analysis: Reviewed base text of StandaloneServer.swift (lines 588-1779) alongside the patch excerpt. The visible change is a refactor: it adds `minimumGrantBytes(_:)` and passes a per-model `minimumGrantBytes` map into `EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants` at four call sites: `reserveKeepsSurvivorsServiceable`, the initial reslice in `resliceAndBuildBundle`, the assistant-floor fallback retry, and `resliceGrowSurvivors`. This only affects KV grant sizing. It touches no auth, attestation, encryption, key handling, cache-at-rest crypto, or lookup naming (T-041 posture unchanged). It adds no new input surface. The security-relevant effects are availability and resource accounting (A-018, T-029) and memory-pressure behavior (TB-007). The change plausibly tightens behavior: grants are computed with serviceability floors, and the existing refusal guard `resliceKeepsSlotsServiceable` is retained. The patch excerpt is truncated (`patch_excerpt_complete` is false), so I did not see the `resliceGrants` implementation in `EngineV2KVSizing`, nor the later hunks around base lines 1228 and 1382. Open integration question: does the new `minimumGrantBytes` parameter in `resliceGrants` make sums of grants exceed the fleet KV budget (the Σ(ceilings) ≤ budget invariant)? That would need review of `EngineV2KVSizing`, which is not in this batch. The shutdown and lifecycle code in the base text is unchanged context, and I found no regression there. No concrete finding qualifies from the supplied evidence.
